The European Commission's AI Office is formally suspended after member states refuse to staff it, citing unresolved liability risks and lack of enforcement authority. This marks the first complete breakdown of an EU-level AI governance body, with functions tentatively reassigned to national agencies under emergency protocols. The move signals that EU-wide coordination has become untenable under sustained political and technical strain.

These tools gain rapid adoption in civil society and some public agencies, creating a grassroots verification layer outside official channels. While limited against frontier models, they restore minimal public trust in locally deployed systems.
